title: Indefinite: Cuideigin
question: What does 'cuideigin' mean?
explanation: 'Cuideigin' means someone; 'rudeigin' is something and 'duine sam bith' with a negative is nobody.

title: Impersonal passive: Chaidh a ràdh
question: What does 'chaidh a ràdh gun tàinig e' mean?
correct: It was said that he came
wrong1: It will be said that he came
wrong2: It was said that he would come
explanation: 'Chaidh a ràdh' is the impersonal passive of 'ràdh': 'it was said'. 'Thuirt e' would make the active 'he said'.

title: Preposition + article: Air an
question: What does 'air an uachdar' mean?
explanation: 'Air' (on) + 'an' (the) gives 'air an uachdar', 'on the surface'. 'Fon uachdar' would be under the surface.

title: Preposition + article: Dhan
question: What does 'dhan taigh' mean?
correct: To the house (do + an contracted as 'dhan')
explanation: 'Dhan' is the fusion of 'do' (to) + 'an' (the).

title: Preposition + article: Anns an
question: What does 'anns an taigh' mean?
explanation: 'Anns an' (ann + s + an) means 'in the'.

title: Preposition: Am measg
question: What does 'am measg' mean?
explanation: 'Am measg' (+ genitive) means 'among'; 'eadar' is 'between' and 'ri taobh' is 'beside'.

title: Preposition: Eadar
question: What does 'eadar Inbhir Nis is Glaschu' mean?
explanation: 'Eadar' (between) + two items + 'is' (and). 'Bho ... gu' would be 'from ... to'.

title: Prepositional pronoun: Agam
question: What does 'tha cù agam' mean?
explanation: 'Agam' is 'aig' + 'mi' (I have). 'Aige' is he has, 'aice' is she has and 'againn' is we have.

title: Pronoun suffix: Sibhse
question: What does 'sibhse' mean?
explanation: '-se' is an emphatic suffix: 'sibhse' = 'you' with emphasis. 'Sinne' is we, 'iadsan' is they and 'ise' is she.

title: Negative marker: Chan fheum
question: What does 'chan fheum mi falbh' mean?
explanation: 'Chan fheum' means 'need not'. 'Chan fhaod' is the form meaning 'must not' or 'may not'.

title: Negative marker: Cha robh àite
question: What does 'cha robh àite aige' mean?
explanation: 'Cha robh' is the negative past of 'bi' and 'aige' means he has: 'he had no place'.

title: Question word: Carson nach
question: What does 'carson nach eil thu a' tighinn?' mean?
explanation: 'Carson' means why, so 'carson nach eil thu a' tighinn?' asks for the reason. 'Nach eil thu a' tighinn?' alone is 'aren't you coming?'.

title: Affirmative: Gun teagamh
question: What does 'gun teagamh' mean?
explanation: 'Gun teagamh' (without doubt) means 'undoubtedly'. 'Theagamh' (perhaps) is a different word.

title: Affirmative: Gu cinnteach
question: What does 'gu cinnteach' mean?
explanation: 'Gu cinnteach' (to certainty) means 'certainly' or 'definitely'.

title: Time: An-dràsta
question: What does 'an-dràsta' mean?
explanation: 'An-dràsta' means 'right now'. 'An-diugh' is today and 'a dh'aithghearr' is soon.

title: Intensifier: Dìreach
question: What does 'dìreach mar sin' mean?
explanation: 'Dìreach' (straight, exact) intensifies: 'dìreach mar sin' = 'exactly like that'.

title: Approximation: Mu
question: What does 'mu chòig mionaidean' mean?
explanation: 'Mu' (about) marks approximation: 'mu chòig mionaidean' = 'about five minutes'.

title: Approximation: Timcheall
question: What does 'timcheall air dà uair' mean?
explanation: 'Timcheall air' (around) marks approximation in time.

title: Degree: Buileach
question: What does 'buileach' mean?
explanation: 'Buileach' is an adverb meaning 'completely' or 'entirely'.

title: Degree: Gu ìre
question: What does 'gu ìre' mean?
explanation: 'Gu ìre' (to an extent) means 'somewhat' or 'to some extent'.

title: Degree: Glè
question: What does 'glè mhath' mean?
explanation: 'Glè' (very) + lenited adjective = high degree. 'Ro mhath' would be too good.

title: Manner: Gu socair
question: What does 'gu socair' mean?
explanation: 'Gu socair' (to softness) means 'gently' or 'quietly'.

title: Manner: Gu luath
question: What does 'gu luath' mean?
explanation: 'Gu luath' (to speed) means 'quickly' or 'rapidly'.

title: Negation: Chan eil mi toilichte
question: What does 'chan eil mi toilichte leis a' bhiadh' mean?
correct: I am not pleased with the food
wrong1: I was not pleased with the food
wrong2: I will not be pleased with the food
wrong3: I am pleased with the food
explanation: 'Chan eil' is the present negative of 'bi', so the whole predicate is negated: 'I am not pleased'.

title: Negative future: Cha tèid
question: What does 'cha tèid mi ann a-màireach' mean?
explanation: 'Cha tèid' is the negative future of 'rach'. 'Cha deach' is past and 'cha rachainn' is conditional.

title: Negation: Duine sam bith
question: What does 'chan eil duine sam bith ann' mean?
explanation: 'Chan eil ... sam bith' creates emphatic negation: 'not anybody at all'. 'Cha robh' would be past and 'cha bhi' would be future.

title: Concessive: Ge b' e cò
question: What does 'ge b' e cò a thig' mean?
explanation: 'Ge b' e' + question word means 'whoever/whatever': 'cò' is who and 'dè' is what.

title: Concessive: Ged a
question: What does 'ged a tha e dona' mean?
explanation: 'Ged a' introduces concessive clauses: 'although'.

title: Conditional: Nan tigeadh tu
question: What does 'nan tigeadh tu' mean?
explanation: 'Nan' + conditional introduces an unreal or hypothetical 'if'.

title: Comparative: Nas ... na
question: What does 'tha e nas àirde na mise' mean?
correct: He is taller than I am
wrong1: He is as tall as I am
wrong3: He is shorter than I am
explanation: 'Nas àirde' is the comparative of 'àrd' and 'na' means 'than'.

title: Superlative: As àirde
question: What does 'is e Iain as àirde' mean?
explanation: 'As àirde' is the superlative of 'àrd': 'the tallest'. 'As ìsle' would be the shortest.

title: Cleft question: Nach ann an seo
question: What does 'nach ann an seo a tha e?' mean?
explanation: 'Nach' makes a negative question and 'an seo' is here. 'An ann an seo a tha e?' would be the positive question.

title: Free relative: Ge b' e dè
question: What does 'ge b' e dè a thuirt e' mean?
explanation: 'Ge b' e dè' means 'whatever' ('dè' = what).

title: Copular negative: Cha b' e
question: What does 'cha b' e sin an fhìrinn' mean?
wrong2: That will not be the truth
explanation: 'Cha b' e' is the negative past of the copula: 'it was not'. 'Chan e' would be present.

title: Copular interrogative: An e ... a bh' ann
question: What does 'an e Iain a bh' ann?' mean?
explanation: 'An e ... a bh' ann?' asks 'was it ...?'. 'A th' ann' would make it present.
